questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD mastery: per-namespace isolation, InitContainer usage, secret/config management, and production-grade guarantees.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer for model pull from Secret
- ConfigMap and Secret usage for runtime parameters
- Probes and HPA for reliability and scale
- Idempotent DB writes to achieve at-least-once delivery
- NetworkPolicy to enforce namespace boundaries

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ns-image-resize
  namespace: <ns>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: image-resize
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: fetch-model
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "download-model.sh"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: model
              mountPath: /models
      containers:
        - name: processor
          image: registry/ns-image-resize:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          envFrom:
            - secretRef: { name: resize-secret }
      volumes:
        - name: model
          emptyDir: {}
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 15
        periodSeconds: 20
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - weight: 100
              podAffinityTerm:
                labelSelector:
                  matchLabels:
                    app: image-resize
                topologyKey: "kubernetes.io/hostname"
  ```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor idempotency and retry behavior?
- What changes if Kafka offset management moves to a separate transactional store?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to coordinate init-time setup with a running app, ensuring idempotent migrations and safe rollbacks in a realistic CKAD scenario.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer orchestration and order
- PVC-mounted data initialization
- Probes for readiness/liveness under patch
- PodDisruptionBudget and graceful shutdown
- Rollback strategies in Kubernetes manifests

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal patch skeleton (illustrative)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: webapp
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: migrate
        image: migrate-image:latest
        command: ["/usr/local/bin/migrate"]
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /data
          name: data
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: webapp:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - mountPath: /data
          name: data
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "200m"
            memory: "256Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: data-pvc
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 10
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: webapp-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: webapp
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you ensure the InitContainer migration runs idempotently across restarts?
- What metrics or events would you monitor to validate rollout safety and rollback effectiveness?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Assess ability to constrain scheduling to hardware and perform safe rolling updates for GPU workloads.

## Key Concepts
- NodeSelector and taints/tolerations
- GPU resource requests/limits
- Readiness/Liveness probes
- RollingUpdate strategy and preStop
- Verification and rollback procedures

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ai-processor
  namespace: ml
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: ai-processor
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ai-processor
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        hardware: gpu
      tolerations:
      - key: hardware
        operator: Equal
        value: gpu
        effect: NoSchedule
      containers:
      - name: ai-processor
        image: your-image:tag
        resources:
          requests:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
            memory: "2Gi"
            cpu: "500m"
          limits:
            nvidia.com/gpu: 1
            memory: "4Gi"
            cpu: "1000m"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /live
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
        lifecycle:
          preStop:
            exec:
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "sleep 5"]
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 1
      maxSurge: 1
```

## Verification Under Load
1. Deploy and verify pods schedule on GPU nodes: `kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide`
2. Check GPU allocation: `kubectl describe nodes | grep nvidia.com/gpu`
3. Load test with concurrent requests while monitoring pod health
4. Verify rolling updates maintain availability: `kubectl rollout status deployment/ai-processor -n ml`
5. Monitor GPU utilization during load: `nvidia-smi` on target nodes

## Rollback Strategy
1. Use deployment revision history: `kubectl rollout history deployment/ai-processor -n ml`
2. Quick rollback: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/ai-processor -n ml`
3. For critical issues, scale to zero then redeploy previous stable version
4. Monitor rollback progress and verify pod health and GPU allocation

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design per-namespace automation with auditability and tight network controls. Image provenance is a critical security concern for multi-tenant environments like Discord or Airbnb, where ensuring container images come from trusted registries is essential.

## Key Concepts
- **CKAD Scheduling**: CronJob for recurring audit tasks
- **Image Provenance**: Registry API integration, image digests (SHA256)
- **Secrets & ConfigMaps**: REGISTRY_TOKEN for authentication, audit-status for state tracking
- **PV-backed Storage**: PVC at /audit for persistent digest reports
- **InitContainers**: Installing required tools (curl, jq) for image inspection
- **Readiness Probes**: Ensuring the pod is ready before accepting traffic
- **Namespace NetworkPolicy**: Restricting egress to only trusted registries

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: image-provenance-audit
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  schedule: "*/30 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: audit-sa
          initContainers:
          - name: tools
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache curl jq"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: audit-volume
              mountPath: /audit
          containers:
          - name: auditor
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "..."]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: audit-volume
              mountPath: /audit
            - name: registry-token
              mountPath: /secrets
              readOnly: true
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command: ["sh", "-c", "[ -f /audit/ready ]"]
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
          volumes:
          - name: audit-volume
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: audit-pvc
          - name: registry-token
            secret:
              secretName: REGISTRY_TOKEN
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: audit-status
  namespace: target-namespace
data:
  last_run: ""
  digest_count: "0"
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: registry-egress
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: registry
```

## Trade-offs Discussion
- **CronJob vs Job**: CronJob provides scheduling but has slight timing drift; use precise timing if required.
- **PVC Size**: Allocate sufficient storage based on pod count and audit frequency.
- **InitContainer Overhead**: Adds startup time but ensures tools are available; consider using a custom image with pre-installed tools.
- **NetworkPolicy Scope**: A permissive egress may be necessary if multiple registries are used; balance security with operational flexibility.
- **ConfigMap Updates**: Frequent updates may cause contention; consider annotation-based status or external database for high-frequency audits.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to compose CKAD primitives into a small, observable application with proper security and observability patterns.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMaps and Secrets for configuration management
- InitContainers and Sidecars for application lifecycle management
- Probes (readiness and liveness) for health monitoring
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for traffic security
- RBAC basics for in-namespace metrics access
- Observability and security trade-offs in containerized applications

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal Deployment sketch
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: python-api
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: python-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: python-api
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-deps
        image: python:3.11-alpine
        command: ['sh', '-c', 'pip install -r /app/requirements.txt']
        volumeMounts:
        - name: app-code
          mountPath: /app
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: python:3.11-alpine
        command: ['python', '/app/main.py']
        env:
        - name: ENABLE_METRICS
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: app-config
              key: ENABLE_METRICS
        - name: API_USERNAME
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: api-credentials
              key: username
        - name: API_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: api-credentials
              key: password
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
        volumeMounts:
        - name: app-code
          mountPath: /app
      - name: cert-rotator
        image: cert-manager/cert-manager-rotator:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: certs
          mountPath: /etc/certs
      volumes:
      - name: app-code
        configMap:
          name: app-code
      - name: certs
        emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-egress
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: monitoring
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 9000
```

## Trade-offs
- **Security vs. Complexity**: NetworkPolicy adds security but increases deployment complexity
- **Resource Overhead**: Sidecar containers double resource requirements for cert management
- **Observability Cost**: Metrics endpoint requires additional monitoring infrastructure
- **InitContainer Impact**: Dependency installation extends pod startup time
- **Namespace Isolation**: Per-namespace design improves security boundaries but requires duplicate configuration management

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests comprehensive CKAD skills including per-namespace isolation, configuration management with ConfigMaps and Secrets, InitContainers for dependency setup, sidecar patterns for auxiliary services, health probes for reliability, RBAC for security, and NetworkPolicy for traffic control.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainers for runtime dependency installation
- ConfigMaps and Secrets for configuration and credential management
- Sidecar containers for TLS certificate rotation
- Readiness and liveness probes for health monitoring
- Namespace isolation and NetworkPolicy for security boundaries
- Dead-letter queue implementation on PVC storage
- At-least-once delivery semantics with batch processing

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: ns-collector
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  initContainers:
  - name: install-deps
    image: alpine:latest
    command: ['sh', '-c', 'apk add --no-cache nats-cli']
  containers:
  - name: collector
    image: collector:latest
    envFrom:
    - configMapRef:
        name: ns-collector-config
    - secretRef:
        name: ns-collector-creds
    readinessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /health
        port: 8080
    livenessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /health
        port: 8080
    volumeMounts:
    - name: dlq-pvc
      mountPath: /dlq
  - name: tls-sidecar
    image: tls-sidecar:latest
    volumeMounts:
    - name: tls-certs
      mountPath: /etc/tls
  volumes:
  - name: dlq-pvc
    persistentVolumeClaim:
      claimName: dlq-pvc
  - name: tls-certs
    secret:
      secretName: tls-certs
```

## Trade-offs
- **At-least-once vs exactly-once**: At-least-once provides simpler implementation but may cause duplicate processing
- **Sidecar overhead**: TLS rotation adds resource consumption but improves security
- **PVC vs temporary storage**: PVC provides persistence but increases complexity and cost
- **NetworkPolicy restrictions**: Improve security but may impact debugging and monitoring capabilities

## Why This Is Asked
This question validates understanding of per-namespace resource governance in Kubernetes. It tests knowledge of how LimitRange and ResourceQuota work together to control pod sizing and cluster resource allocation.

## Key Concepts
- **LimitRange**: Sets default requests/limits applied to Pods that don't specify resources
- **ResourceQuota**: Enforces hard limits on total namespace resource consumption
- **Policy alignment**: Ensuring Deployments specify resources matching namespace defaults
- **Verification**: Testing policy enforcement with intentional over-allocation
- **Rollback**: Strategy for removing or scaling back resources when policies need adjustment

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: analytics-lr
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  limits:
  - type: Container
    default:
      cpu: "200m"
      memory: 256Mi
    defaultRequest:
      cpu: "100m"
      memory: 128Mi
```
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: analytics-quo
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  hard:
    cpu: "400m"
    memory: 512Mi
    requests.storage: "1Gi"
```
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: reporter
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: reporter
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "200m"
            memory: "256Mi"
```
## Verification Commands
```bash
kubectl apply -f limitrange.yaml
kubectl apply -f quota.yaml
kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml
kubectl describe resourcequota analytics-quo -n analytics
kubectl run overload-test --image=busybox --restart=Never --requests=cpu=500m,memory=600Mi --dry-run=server
```
## Rollback Strategy
```bash
kubectl delete -f quota.yaml
kubectl delete -f limitrange.yaml
kubectl scale deployment reporter --replicas=0 -n analytics
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD ability to implement per-namespace GitOps, use InitContainers, ConfigMaps, PVCs, and NetworkPolicy; validates YAML tooling, apply flow, and status reporting.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace GitOps design patterns
- InitContainer provisioning and tool installation
- YAML validation with kubeval and yamllint
- ConfigMap and Secret usage for configuration
- PVC-based log streaming and persistence
- Namespace-scoped NetworkPolicy for egress control
- Drift detection and status reporting via ConfigMap

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton for a per-namespace GitOps runner
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gitops-runner
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gitops-runner
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gitops-runner
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: git-clone
        image: alpine/git:latest
        env:
        - name: REPO_URL
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: repo-url
        - name: TARGET_PATH
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: gitops-config
              key: target-path
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          apk add --no-cache git yq
          git clone $(REPO_URL) /workspace/repo
          cd /workspace/repo
          yq eval '.spec.path = "$(TARGET_PATH)"' . > manifests.yaml
      containers:
      - name: validator
        image: kubeval/kubeval:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
        command:
        - /bin/sh
        - -c
        - |
          kubeval /workspace/manifests.yaml > /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          yamllint -d relaxed /workspace/manifests.yaml >> /logs/validation.log 2>&1
          kubectl apply -f /workspace/manifests.yaml --namespace=$(NAMESPACE)
          kubectl get -f /workspace/manifests.yaml -o jsonpath='{.status}' > /gitops-status
      volumes:
      - name: workspace
        emptyDir: {}
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: gitops-logs
```

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-backup
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: installer
              image: busybox
              command:
                - /bin/sh
                - -c
                - apk add --no-cache tar pigz
          containers:
            - name: backup
              image: alpine:3.18
              command:
                - /bin/sh
                - -c
                - tar -czf /backup/namespace-$(date +%F-%H%M).tar.gz -C /data .
              volumeMounts:
                - name: data
                  mountPath: /data
                - name: backup
                  mountPath: /backup
              readinessProbe:
                exec:
                  command:
                    - cat
                    - /tmp/healthy
                initialDelaySeconds: 30
                periodSeconds: 60
              livenessProbe:
                httpGet:
                  path: /healthz
                  port: 8080
          volumes:
            - name: data
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: data-pvc
            - name: backup
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: backup-pvc
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

metadata:

      labels:
        app: canary-health-tester

        - name: installer
